pages.description: England manager Thomas Tuchel omits Josh King, James Garner and Jarrad Branthwaite from his squad to face Spain on Sunday night.
pages.text: England team news: Thomas Tuchel omits Jarrad Branthwaite, James Garner and Josh King for Spain game - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, James Garner played as a substitute against Croatia on Thursday, while Jarrad Branthwaite and Josh King were unused By Sami Mokbel Senior football correspondent Published 15 November 2026 England manager Thomas Tuchel has omitted Josh King, James Garner and Jarrad Branthwaite from his squad to face world champions Spain in Madrid on Sunday night. England travelled to Spain with a squad of 26 players but Uefa rules state that only 23 players can be selected in a matchday squad for Nations League games The return to fitness of Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence - who missed Thursday's win over Croatia - has been a contributing factor in the trio's omission. Arsenal defender Konsa could come straight back into the starting XI while James Trafford will replace Jordan Pickford in goal. Garner replaced Declan Rice in the 77th minute of the 2-1 victory over Croatia at Wembley, scoring a goal that was subsequently disallowed, while Everton team-mate Branthwaite and Fulham's King were unused substitutes. King received his first senior call-up for the two final Nations League fixtures in Group A3, but the midfielder, 19, will not feature in this international window. However, fellow first-time call-ups Jobe Bellingham and James Hill are included. pages.text: England v Australia: Player-coach rift report will only galvanise us - George - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Jamie George (left) and captain Maro Itoje (right) are part of Steve Borthwick's senior leadership group By Mike Henson BBC Sport rugby union news reporter Published 6 November 2026 England hooker Jamie George says the squad are "really upset" by a newspaper article claiming the end of their summer tour was marked by player unrest over head coach Steve Borthwick's leadership. A report in the Times , external says unhappy players wanted summit talks with Borthwick and Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney in Argentina in July. It alleges there are disagreements among Borthwick's wider coaching group, which has been subject to frequent change in his nearly four years in charge, and concerns over the head coach's man-management skills. England meet Australia in the Nations Championship on Sunday at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham, with George querying the timing of the article as well as its contents. The Saracens hooker, who was made England captain by Borthwick in 2024 before the role passed to Maro Itoje 12 months later, said that he did not recognise the situation described by the article. "I can tell you that a lot of it's untrue," George told Rugby Union Weekly. "We, as a squad, are incredibly disappointed by it. pages.text: England v Japan: Max Ojomoh must marry talent and toughness - Steve Borthwick - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Ojomoh put in superb performance against Argentina last autumn, scoring a try in a 27-23 win By Chris Jones Rugby union correspondent Published 13 November 2026 Centre Max Ojomoh - labelled "one of the most talented players in English rugby" - has been challenged to produce a relentless and physical performance against Japan on Saturday. The Bath man burst on to the international scene in a man-of-the-match display against Argentina at the end of 2025, but has not played for his country in the 12 months since. Ojomoh was initially left out of Steve Borthwick's wider training squad but after starring for the 'A' team has been catapulted back into the England number 12 shirt and with it World Cup contention. "Max is one of the most talented players in English rugby," boss Steve Borthwick told BBC Sport. "His ability to see space and distribute, to hide where he is going to pass and to pass short or long, that's a rare skill." However Borthwick says the position of centre has changed markedly over the years, and it now requires a level of unyielding physical output to go with a wide skill-set. "You have to be incredibly skilled in that position, but it demands a skill and toughness it previously probably didn't," he explained. "It used to be a second receiver, that second pair of eyes, the distribution skills and the potential kicking skills. pages.description: New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie demands a reaction against England, as he acknowledges the All Blacks "let the country down" by losing to Wales.
pages.text: England v New Zealand: All Blacks coach Dave Rennie says team 'let the country down' in Wales defeat - BBC Sport Figure caption, Highlights: Wales beat New Zealand for first time in 73 years By Chris Jones Rugby union correspondent Published 16 November 2026 New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie has demanded a reaction against England on Saturday after saying the All Blacks "let the country down" in their historic defeat by Wales. In one of the great upsets of the professional era, New Zealand lost 35-28 in Cardiff at the weekend, a first defeat against the Welsh in 73 years. New Zealand will face an in-form England in Twickenham as they look to avoid back-to-back Nations Championship losses, with Rennie vowing not to brush the Wales result "under the carpet". "It's important we poke each other in the chest at the start of the week," Rennie said. "You have to front up and take things on the chin, all of us. Come Saturday, our mindset will be fully on England and our job is to perform. "We will be highly motivated for the weekend, but we won't brush the [Wales] result under the carpet. "[The players] are feeling it. They know we let ourselves down and we let the country down." pages.text: England v New Zealand: Jack van Poortvliet on 2022 All Blacks nightmare - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Jack van Poortvliet, who made a try-scoring debut against Australia in 2022, has won 29 Test caps By Mike Henson , BBC Sport rugby union news reporter and Sara Orchard , Rugby union commentator Published 18 November 2026 A mocking pat on the back from Codie Taylor. A close-up of his own face on the Twickenham big screen. A painful inquest under the sticks. Jack van Poortvliet's first meeting with New Zealand was only four minutes old when it curdled sour. In November 2022 Van Poortvliet, then 21, was winning only his sixth cap. Sharing the scrum-half duties with England veterans Ben Youngs and Richard Wigglesworth, he had been a key part in Leicester's run to the Premiership title the previous season. Van Poortvliet was touted as the next big thing at Test level too. But, off an early England line-out, Van Poortvliet, focused on Owen Farrell's hands, failed to spot Dalton Papali'i flying up out of the line. The All Black flanker picked off the interception and cantered in for the game's opening try. Van Poortvliet's afternoon ended after 54 minutes. With England trailing 22-6, his final act was a knock-on after being harried by Brodie Retallick at the back of a breakdown. His mistake squandered a prime attacking position. pages.description: Centre Seb Atkinson is set to return to the England backline for a "dream" encounter with the All Blacks on Saturday.
pages.text: England v New Zealand: Seb Atkinson 'ticking off wishes and dreams' as All Blacks loom - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Atkinson has won eight England caps since making his Test debut in July 2025 By Chris Jones Rugby union correspondent Published 17 November 2026 England centre Seb Atkinson says he is living a childhood dream as he prepares to face New Zealand in Twickenham on Saturday. The Gloucester pivot has recovered from a hip knock and is set to return to the starting XV at number 12 for the visit of the wounded All Blacks. For Atkinson, this weekend's game comes a fortnight after he made his first Allianz Stadium appearance with England in the 45-22 thumping of Australia. "It's sort of ticking off wishes and dreams that you have as a young aspiring rugby player," Atkinson told BBC Sport. "Watching [England against New Zealand in 2012] when Manu [Tuilagi] scored that try and set up that try, the big performance in the semi-final of the World Cup a few years ago [in 2019]. "And obviously I was frustrated to not be available last year when the team put in a good performance. "So a lot of things spring to mind and to be able to be out there and show what I can do on that stage will be really exciting for me personally." pages.text: England women's manager Sarina Wiegman signs two-year contract extension - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Sarina Wiegman has been in charge of England for more than five years By Paul Battison BBC Sport Journalist Published 19 October 2026 England manager Sarina Wiegman has signed a two-year contract extension with the Lionesses. The 56-year-old's previous deal was due to expire after next summer's World Cup, but her new contract will run until the end of Euro 2029. Dutchwoman Wiegman guided England to their second straight European Championship title with victory over Spain in the Euro 2025 final. The victory meant the Lionesses became the first England team - women's or men's - to win a major trophy on foreign soil. "I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football," said Wiegman. "Working for a world-class organisation like The FA, and alongside so many people dedicated to winning England teams and the growth of our game, excites me every day." England thrashed Greece 8-1 on aggregate last week to qualify for round two of the World Cup play-offs, where they will face Ukraine. Should the Lionesses win that two-legged tie, they will qualify for next summer's World Cup in Brazil. "My main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come," Wiegman added. "We have an important job to do to confirm our place in Brazil, and hopefully we can do that and give the country another special summer to remember next year." Wiegman replaced Phil Neville

Enhanced Geothermal Systems Enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) , or human-made geothermal energy, holds the potential to power American homes and businesses nationwide and is the next frontier for geothermal energy deployment What is an Enhanced Geothermal System (EGS)? A naturally occurring geothermal system, known as a hydrothermal system , requires three key elements to generate electricity: heat, fluid, and permeability, which is when fluid can move freely through the underground rock. In many areas, however, the underground rock is hot but there is not enough natural permeability or fluids present. In those cases, an enhanced geothermal system (EGS) can be used to create a human-made reservoir to tap that heat for energy. In an EGS, fluid is injected deep underground under carefully controlled conditions to create new fractures and cause pre-existing fractures to re-open, creating permeability. Increased permeability allows fluid to circulate throughout the more fractured hot rock, and the fluid becomes hot as it circulates. Operators pump the hot water up to the surface, where it generates electricity for the grid. Watch a video to learn more about the steps and benefits in EGS development . With the outbreak of the Civil War in 1861, enslaved African Americans saw the war as opportunity to emancipate themselves. When President Lincoln authorized the Emancipation Proclamation, formerly enslaved African American men joined the Union army to fight for the full emancipation of their race. Massachusetts Institute of Technology has always been associated with major scientific and technological breakthroughs. But the breakthroughs alone do not explain the impact that MIT has had on the world. For that we have to look at entrepreneurship, which starts with the “Mens et Manus” (Mind and Hand) slogan on the Great Seal of MIT. For faculty, students, and alumni, MIT is all about making discoveries and inventions and then applying these discoveries and inventions to solve real problems. In a very tangible way, MIT faculty and graduates invent the future, and entrepreneurship—the building of new businesses—is often the road to that future. Watch this video introduction to entrepreneurship at MIT. The report “ Entrepreneurship and Innovation at MIT ” examines the impact of MIT graduates who have founded and built for-profit companies. The report estimates that, as of 2014, living MIT alumni have launched more than 30,000 active companies, creating some 4.6 million jobs and generating $1.9 trillion in annual revenue. The cumulative result is the equivalent of the 10th largest economy in the world. This rich legacy of high-impact companies spans a wide range of industries; recent examples include A123 Systems, Akamai, iRobot, InVivo Therapeutics and Dropbox. They are most useful when you have a variable that can take one of a limited selection of values. For example, the days of the week: >>> from enum import Enum >>> class Weekday ( Enum ): ... MONDAY = 1 ... TUESDAY = 2 ... WEDNESDAY = 3 ... THURSDAY = 4 ... FRIDAY = 5 ... SATURDAY = 6 ... SUNDAY = 7 Or perhaps the RGB primary colors: >>> from enum import Enum >>> class Color ( Enum ): ... RED = 1 ... GREEN = 2 ... BLUE = 3 As you can see, creating an Enum is as simple as writing a class that inherits from Enum itself. Note Case of Enum Members Because Enums are used to represent constants, and to help avoid issues with name clashes between mixin-class methods/attributes and enum names, we strongly recommend using UPPER_CASE names for members, and will be using that style in our examples. Depending on the nature of the enum a member’s value may or may not be important, but either way that value can be used to get the corresponding member: >>> Weekday ( 3 ) <Weekday.WEDNESDAY: 3> As you can see, the repr() of a member shows the enum name, the member name, and the value. Environmental and Legacy Management The Office of Environmental Management’s (EM) mission is to complete the safe cleanup of environmental legacy waste resulting from decades of nuclear weapons development and nuclear energy research. Since its formation in 1989, the Environmental Management program has tackled one of the largest environmental cleanup efforts in the world — addressing decades of nuclear weapons production and government-sponsored nuclear energy research in the United States. DOE established the Office of Legacy Management on Dec. 15, 2003, to fulfill the department’s post-closure responsibilities by providing long-term surveillance and maintenance, records management, benefits continuity, property management, and land use planning. Presently, Legacy Management manages over 100 legacy sites in 29 states and Puerto Rico. pages.text: Environmental Management Systems | Corporate Environmental Responsibility | FAO Share Close Corporate Environmental Responsibility Environmental Management Systems The Environmental Management System (EMS) is a structured framework that helps FAO manage its environmental responsibilities, reduce environmental impacts, and ensure compliance with regulations in a systematic way. EMS supports continuous, long term improvement in environmental performance. In line with ISO 14001 standards, FAO has implemented an EMS at Headquarters and at the Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, and is progressively extending it to other decentralized offices while strengthening environmental governance at corporate level. The EMS integrates environmental considerations into everyday office activities. While implementation timelines may vary depending on resources and capacity, the framework remains consistent and follows four core phases: Plan – Do – Check – Act.

pages.text: Environmental Sustainability Smithsonian Magazine Skip to main content Environmental Sustainability Sustainability means working to protect our natural resources for future generations. We understand that recycling is inherently good and is fundamental to a healthy environment and society. But it is important to separate the issue of improving collection rates from how that recycled material is then used. Simply dictating that recycled fiber should go into magazine paper overlooks the fact that it could be put to far more efficient and sustainable use in other products. In the past decade, the production of printing and writing papers in North American has dropped by nearly 50% at the same time that exports of recycled paper to China have increased significantly. As a result, despite overall increases in paper recovery rates in the United States, the availability of recycled fiber suitable for use in magazine grades has actually decreased. Given this growing shortage of suitable recycled fiber, it is important to insure that the recycled fiber that is available is put to the best use. It’s not always the right choice to say it should be used in every instance. For example, when recycled fiber is used in certain packaging materials (like recycled paperboard) nearly 100% of the recycled material can be used; however, when recycled fiber is used for magazine paper typically only 70% of the recycled material is usable. This effort is part of EPA’s comprehensive, lifecycle-based strategy to address PFAS and Make America Healthy Again. EPA is taking a radically transparent approach by ensuring robust input is gathered to inform next steps. Eligibility for EPSCoR participation was limited to those jurisdictions that had historically received lesser amounts of federal R&D funding and had demonstrated a commitment to developing their research bases and improving the quality of science and engineering research conducted at their universities and colleges. In Fiscal Year 1992, the Interagency Coordinating Committee, or EICC, was established among the federal agencies with EPSCoR or EPSCoR-like programs. The major objectives of the EICC focus on improving coordination among and between the federal agencies in implementing EPSCoR and EPSCoR-like programs consistent with the policies of those agencies. pages.description: W3C的出版维护工作组一直在默默推进EPUB3标准的又一次更新，我们很高兴与大家分享我们的工作进展。我们的目标不仅是维护EPUB标准，更要尽力让它跟上行业需求，而这次更新正是如此。你现有的电子书无需改动——只要它们符合旧版EPUB，就同样符合EPUB 3.4。你今天创建的内容也会自动符合。
pages.text: EPUB 3.4带着“滚动布局”来啦 | 2026 | 博客 | W3C 转到内容 EPUB 3.4带着“滚动布局”来啦 Part of 无障碍 作者及发布日期 由: Wendy Reid（W3C出版标准维护工作组特邀专家） 发布: 2026年10月12日 W3C的 出版标准维护工作组 一直在默默推进EPUB3标准的又一次更新，我们很高兴与大家分享我们的工作进展。我们的目标不仅是维护EPUB标准，更要尽力让它紧跟行业需求，而这次更新正是如此。 在介绍更新内容之前，我们想提醒大家：我们的首要原则是向后兼容，也就是说，EPUB3的任何更新都不能让此前创建的文件失效。你现有的电子书无需改动——只要它们符合旧版EPUB，就同样符合 EPUB 3.4 。你今天创建的内容只要通过验证，就会自动符合EPUB 3.4。 EPUB 3.4涵盖核心规范、阅读系统规范，并更新了EPUB无障碍1.2版规范。目前，这些文档正处于W3C标准化流程的候选推荐标准阶段，也就是说，我们正在测试规范、征集实现者的反馈，并确保各项修订在正式发布前足够稳定。如果你是阅读系统或工具开发者，我们非常期待听到你的意见。如需测试该规范，可在 测试网站 上了解更多信息。 这是W3C会员单位Kadokawa在其Publus阅读器上进行的滚动布局演示。 引入滚动布局 过去几年，全球出版业最令人瞩目的趋势之一，就是“条漫”（webtoon）的迅速崛起。这是一种源自韩国的流行漫画形式。条漫通常是分集连载的数字漫画，阅读方向是垂直的，而不是像日漫或欧美漫画那样横向阅读。它们专为在智能手机上轻松阅读而设计，整部作品由一长条垂直图像拼接而成。此前，条漫只能局限于专门的阅读应用或网站，因为EPUB之类的格式并不支持它们。而在EPUB 3.4中，我们改变了这一局面。 我们新增了一个 rendition:layout 取值： roll 。滚动布局会告诉阅读系统：渲染时，每个书脊（spine）项都应铺满视口宽度，并按顺序依次显示，项与项之间不留空隙。滚动布局仅适用于固定布局文档，且不受其他固定布局渲染选项（如 rendition:page-spread ）或spine级布局覆盖（如 rendition:layout-reflowable ）的控制。滚动布局与固定布局EPUB面临同样的无障碍难题，我们建议参阅关于 固定布局无障碍 的文档。 这是一段40秒的EPUB滚动布局功能演示视频，由W3C会员Kadokawa基于其Publus阅读器提供。 EPUB 3.4还有哪些变化？ 与以往的标准更新一样，我们着重让规范更易懂、更清晰，并与行业实践保持一致。具体包括：为图像、音频和视频新增内容类型或编解码器，例如AVIF、JPEG XL和OPUS；完善无障碍元数据，确保为用户提供最准确的信息；新增用于联系邮箱的无障碍元数据字段。和以往的修订一样，我们也做了一些清理工作。 10月11日，EPUB 3就满15年了，这些年间发生了很大变化。走过15年历程，我们可以回头看看哪些做法行之有效，哪些未能奏效。在EPUB 3.4中，你会看到不少特性被移入我们所说的“过时”特性，并分为“陈旧”和“废弃”两类。 陈旧特性 陈旧特性属于遗留特性，我们不鼓励作者和开发者在新的作品中继续使用，但阅读系统必须继续支持。这样分类既能确保现有EPUB文件依然有效、可读，又不会助长在现代内容中沿用陈旧做法。 在EPUB 3.4中被列为陈旧的特性之一是字体混淆，它依赖的加密功能已不再被推荐。我们鼓励EPUB创作者改用WOFF2等现代字体格式。有关哪些内容被认定为陈旧，以及这些特性的可能替代方案，可在 规范 的“陈旧特性”（Outdated features）一节中查看。 废弃特性 废弃特性是指在阅读系统或EPUB出版物中几乎没有支持的特性。当某项特性被废弃时
